main_text.p: נָחָה Duxit, Adduxit, Abduxit, Deduxit: Præ-ter. נְחַנִי Deduxit me, Genes.24.27. Imperat. נְחֵה אֶת־הָעָם Deduc populum istum, Exod.32.34. Hiph. Præter. הִנְחַנִי Duxit me, Genes.24.48.

מִנְחָה [?] f. Munus, Oblatio, ab Adducendo, ut quidam volunt, forma מַצָּה Præceptum: aut quia pluralem ejus absolutum Rabbini efferunt מִנְחוֹת, Mem cum Scheva, idem radicale esse censetur, ad formam נַעֲרָה [?], unde Plural. גִּבְעוֹת [?]: si autem מ esset servile, diceretur מִנְחוֹת ad formam מִצְוֹת, vide ergo illud in מנח.

נָחַל Possedit, Possessor fuit vel factus est, Possessionem habuit, Possidendum accepit. Semel, Possidendum dedit vel distribuit, ut Numer.34.17. Futur. יִנְחְלוּ כָּבוֹד חֲכָמִים Gloriam sapientes possidebunt, Proverb.3.35. In Pih. נִחֵל Possidere fecit, Possidendum tradidit, Possessionem distribuit: Præter. אֲשֶׁר נְחַל Quae possidenda tradidit, Jos.13.32. נְחַלוּ אוֹתָם Quae possidenda tradiderunt illis, Jos.14.1. Reliqua, quae hujus Præteriti formam habent, vide in חלל. Hiph. Præterit. הִנְחַלְתִּי אֶת־אֲבֹתֵיכֶם Possidere feci patres vestros, Jer.3. v.18. &c. Hoph. Præt. הִנְחַלְתִּי Effectum est ut possideam, Job.7. v.3. Hithp. הִתְנַחֵל Possessorem se constituit, Possessionem adiit: Præter. וְהִתְנַחֲלוּ Et constituent se possessores eorum, Jesa.14.2. וְהִתְנַחֲלֻם Constituetis vos possessores, Levit.25.46. Infinit. עַד־הִתְנַחֵל Donec constituerint se possessores, Num.32.18. Futur. יִתְנַחֲלוּ Possessionem adibit, Num.34.13.

נַחֲלָה f. Possessio: Semel irregulariter, נַחֲלַת Psal.16.6. cui simile in זָמַר [?] & in מְנוּרָה [?]: Constructo. נַחֲלַת שָׂדֶה Possessionem agri, Numer.16.14. Aff. נַחֲלָתוֹ Possessio ejus, Deut.18.2. נַחֲלָתָם Possessiones vestræ, Psal.105.11. Plural. הַנַּחֲלוֹת Possessiones, Jos.19.50.

page.notes: Hebrew forms marked [?] are uncertain on the scan (vowel points and some consonants at the small type size). The large Hebrew headwords are set in larger type but are part of the entry paragraphs, so they are not given as headings. Hyphens at line ends (Præ-ter) are printed. The Hebrew of the second entry, especially the plural form, is hard to read. Long s is written as s.
